question: A square and a circle have equal perimeter. Find the ratio of the square’s area to the circle’s area.

solution.asked: Express both areas using the common perimeter.
steps: The square side is P/4, giving area P²/16.
The circle radius is P/(2π), giving area P²/(4π).
commonMistakes: Equal perimeter does not imply equal area.

hints: Identify the conditions under which isoperimetric comparison applies.
Start from $ A_{sq}=P^2/16,\quad A_{circ}=P^2/(4\pi) $.

verification.method: Construct actual equal-perimeter square/circle dimensions and compare their areas. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: For nonnegative data values, which transformations necessarily produce the stated effect?

options.text: Adding 5 to every value adds 5 to the mean
Adding 5 to every value adds 5 to the standard deviation
Multiplying every value by 2 multiplies standard deviation by 2
Multiplying every value by 2 multiplies variance by 2

given: Finite data set with population variance convention
solution.asked: Select valid location and scale rules.
steps: A constant shift moves the mean but leaves all centered deviations unchanged.
A factor 2 doubles deviations and standard deviation, while quadrupling variance.
commonMistakes: Variance scales quadratically, whereas standard deviation scales linearly.

hints: Identify the conditions under which statistics under affine transformations applies.
Start from $ E[aX+b]=aE[X]+b,\quad Var(aX+b)=a^2Var(X) $.

verification.method: Affine central-moment algebra; explicit shifted/scaled nonconstant data checks. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: A positive number is selected uniformly from integers 1 to 30. Find the probability it is divisible by 2 or by 3.

solution.asked: Count the union without double-counting multiples of 6.
steps: There are 15 multiples of 2 and 10 multiples of 3.
Union count is 15+10−5=20, so probability is 20/30=2/3.
